candidates.fit: usbc: 16P power-only pinout (CC1/CC2, SBU1/2, DP1/DN1, VBUS x4, GND x4) at 20V/5A, deep stock, and the ONLY candidate with a ready-made KiCad footprint (Connector_USB.pretty/USB_C_Receptacle_HRO_TYPE-C-31-M-12.kicad_mod, verified in this image), which removes the pulled-footprint DRC-error class this repo's LEARNINGS documents for 16P USB-C parts. That footprint's own pads confirm the shield/ground return is 4x plated THT oval pads ("SH") plus 2x NPTH alignment holes, not full SMD.

usbc: cheapest and highest-stock 16P option (30V/3A, still >>1A design current), but no vendor-specific KiCad footprint ships in the library - would need a pulled/custom footprint. Vendor drawing (pulled and read directly) shows the same hybrid construction as the HRO part: 16 SMD signal pads plus 2x 0.65mm-dia THT shield/mounting legs at the housing ends.

usbc: same SHOU HAN 16P family as C393939 (3A/5V), alternate SKU with no datasheet on file at LCSC; single-source risk is the same pulled-footprint gap as C393939 with less stock depth, kept only as a price-tier alternate.
usbc: BXCONN clone, cheapest unit price found but stock (903) is thin for a part with no datasheet on file; adequate for a 5-board build, not a reorder-safe choice.

jst_sh: genuine JST SH 1.0mm 4-pin, right-angle/horizontal (correct Qwiic/STEMMA-QT mating orientation); exact KiCad footprint ships in Connector_JST.pretty as JST_SH_SM04B-SRSS-TB_1x04-1MP_P1.00mm_Horizontal. Highest price of the three but the reference part the clones are copied from.

jst_sh: XYECONN clone of the JST part, same body/pinout family so it should sit in the genuine-part KiCad footprint; 5.4x cheaper than JST-branded, moderate stock. No datasheet on file - JST's own drawing is the fallback reference for dimension checks.
jst_sh: hanxia clone, near-identical price/stock to the XYECONN clone; kept as a second-source alternate in case one clone line goes out of stock.

header: 1x4 THT male pin header for SWD/UART, ships DNP (JLC economy PCBA is SMT-only per requirements.md 7); generic part, matches KiCad's standard PinHeader_1x04_P2.54mm_Vertical footprint (any 2.54mm 1x4 header is mechanically interchangeable). Best stock of the three checked.
header: JXTCONN generic 1x4 header, cheapest of the three (moot for a DNP line item); listed for the BOM do-not-populate reference only.
header: Ckmtw generic 1x4 header, higher-temp rated (-40..105C) alternate with a real datasheet on file if a documented part is preferred for the DNP BOM line.

button: only JLC Basic tactile switch found (no assembly setup fee), huge stock, cheapest of the four; footprint is 5.1x5.1mm, larger than the brief's named 3x2.5/4.2x3.2mm classes - flagged size trade-off, but this is one of the most heavily reused JLC Basic buttons with no known footprint/DRC issues.
button: closest match to the brief's small-size class (4x3mm vs the named 3x2.5/4.2x3.2mm), Extended but deep stock and cheap; 2-pin SPST tab-terminal part, no datasheet on file at LCSC.

candidates.mpn: TS263065A 340gf SX BD SMD Tactile Switch
candidates.fit: button: smallest footprint AND lowest profile (0.65mm) of the four, closely matches the brief's 3x2.5mm class - but this exact MPN is a documented risk in this repo's LEARNINGS (2026-07-28, easyeda2kicad/parts): its name (spaces + slash-unsafe characters) has caused lib_pull to silently fail the symbol pull while reporting success. If picked, verify the pulled symbol by hand before relying on lib_pull's status.

button: smallest footprint of the four and 4-pin (more mechanically stable than 2-pin tab types), but stock is only 86 pieces - covers a 5-board build with zero margin for rework/rejects, not reorder-safe.

led: red, JLC Basic, huge stock, cheapest of the family. Vf 1.8-2.4V typ (spec'd at IF=20mA only: Iv 145-300mcd, typ ~220mcd). Datasheet's Iv-vs-If curve is sub-linear at low current; reading it gives roughly 80-110mcd @ 5mA and 30-45mcd @ 2mA (curve-read estimate, not a bin spec) - architect should size the series resistor from the 1.8-2.4V Vf range, not the 20mA Iv number, since this board should run LEDs well below 20mA.

led: white (CCT 40000-100000K, i.e. very cool/bluish-white), JLC Basic, deep stock. Directly spec'd at IF=5mA: Iv 145-360mcd (typ ~250mcd), Vf 2.6-3.1V typ. At 2mA expect roughly 40-60% of the 5mA value (InGaN dies are closer to linear at low current than the red AlGaInP die) - no direct 2mA point in the datasheet.

led: emerald green, Extended, same family/price as white. Directly spec'd at IF=5mA: Iv 210-430mcd (typ ~300mcd), Vf 2.6-3.1V typ - the brightest of the family at 5mA, good user-LED candidate if Extended is acceptable (brief allows Extended for brief-named connector/indicator parts).
led: blue, Extended, same family. Directly spec'd at IF=5mA: Iv 70-175mcd (typ ~120mcd), Vf 2.6-3.1V typ - dimmest of the family at 5mA; listed for color-choice completeness only.
